text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:

- Former East German Politburo member Guenter Schabowski admits East German leadership has political and moral guilt for shooting deaths of refugees fleeing west at Berlin Wall and German-German border.
- Serious financial damage caused by fraud in Hamburg healthcare system. Police investigating more than 80 cases of fraud.
- French President Jacque Chirac praises friendship with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl. Says France will reach its goal of qualifying for the euro on time.
- German Labour Office in Nuremberg forced to sell for the first time in its history liabilities worth 1.8 billion marks in order to reduce its deficit.
- Stronger dollar helps German export industry. Germany.'s international competitive position strengthened. The higher dollar improves the earnings position of German companies.

- Germany supports plans by U.N. Secretary-General to reform the U.N.'s bureacracy. Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel says Germany will back efforts to reform the institution and make it - Dresdner Bank plans to ask historians to examine the bank's activities during World War Two.

- FDP chief Wolfgang Gerhardt urges Chancellor's Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats to be more courageous. He admits the government is in a trough at the moment. He said the gridlock blocking reform is not so much a result of mistakes rather a lack of decisions.
- Water levels on the Oder river near record levels. The river reaches its highest level since 1930. Bridges over the river into Poland have already been closed.

- Coalition negotiating a compromise on taxes. Some elements of SPD counter offers should be adapted, coalition officials suggest. Rather than planning how to portray in the best possible light the collapse of tax reform, the coalition should first try to portray the SPD as blocker of the reforms.
- German President Roman Herzog says construction of federal president's office building in Berlin a "signal" for the government's planned move to Berlin in 1999.
